elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"

elements.element: Vendor assigns deliverables/work product to Customer
elements.evidence: "Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon creation"
"Vendor retains Vendor Technology as provided in Section 14.3"; Vendor Technology = "Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates..."

elements.element: Licence to Customer of any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: Redline contains no embedded-IP licence; only "Vendor retains Vendor Technology as provided in Section 14.3."

elements.element: That licence is perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free
elements.evidence: No licence language at all in the revised 14.2; prior "revocable, non-transferable licence" sentence was deleted without replacement grant

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: Clause is silent on Customer Data; only definitional carve-out "Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; Deliverables "exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how"

elements.element: Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to deliverables
elements.evidence: No licence grant survives; the licence sentence was replaced by an assignment

elements.element: Licence rights to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business
elements.evidence: No use/modify/sublicense language appears in the rendered clause

offending_extra_words: Vendor retains Vendor Technology as provided in Section 14.3.
and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon creation
reasons: Preferred level is incomplete: the assignment and Vendor pre-existing IP retention are secured, but there is no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables, so Customer-owned Deliverables containing Vendor Technology remain unlicensed.
The clause is silent on Customer's retention of rights in Customer Data; only a definitional carve-out exists, which is not an affirmative ownership statement.
Fallback is not satisfied either (no use/modify/sublicense licence), and the two levels cannot be mixed.

Minimality fails: the official gate records a 0.714 changed-character ratio; flipping the ownership operator and adding a short assignment phrase would have sufficed, and the added "Vendor retains Vendor Technology as provided in Section 14.3" duplicates protection already given by Section 14.3 and the Deliverable/Vendor Technology definitions.

Suggested fix: keep the ownership flip and assignment, delete the redundant Section 14.3 restatement, and add a short embedded-IP licence, e.g. "Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in a Deliverable."
